stories.title: Unexpected spin effect lets electric currents switch antiferromagnets at room temperature
stories.desc: Researchers have discovered a physical effect that expands the fundamental understanding of how electric currents interact with magnetism, revealing an unexpected way to manipulate the magnetic state of antiferromagnetic materials. A research team led by Northwestern Engineering's Pedram Khalili…

stories.title: The secret of 'strange metals' may lie in quantum statistics, not collisions
stories.desc: In an ordinary metal, electrons behave like well-defined particles that occasionally bump into imperfections or vibrations of the crystal. Many materials with strong electron–electron interactions, including the copper-oxide (cuprate) superconductors, break these rules. In these "strange metals,"…

stories.title: Unusual magnetism revealed in a simple metal's electron spins
stories.desc: Magnets are usually associated with a familiar property: they produce a magnetic field because the magnetic moments of their electrons align. But nature allows much more unusual forms of magnetic order. An international research team has now identified compelling experimental evidence for p-wave…

stories.title: X-rays tear water apart before its electrons can relax
stories.desc: A single X‑ray photon can break both O–H bonds in a water molecule within a few femtoseconds (quadrillionths of a second), creating neutral atomic oxygen. As shown by a study published in the journal Physical Review Letters, this breakup happens before the electrons finish relaxing, revealing an…

stories.title: 'PAC-MAN' capsules that gobble up particles in turbulent water show promise for filtration and drug delivery
stories.desc: Scientists have created hollow capsules with single openings that can selectively filter particles thanks to the turbulence in surrounding waters—at times, ingesting particles like PAC-MAN eating up dots.

stories.title: Exquisite X-rays and dynamic compression initiate a new era of physics experiments on plutonium
stories.desc: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), Argonne National Laboratory (ANL) and Washington State University (WSU) have conducted the first dynamic compression experiments on plutonium at a national light source facility, the Dynamic Compression Sector (DCS).

stories.title: Long DNA strands turn chaotic fluid motion into a steady rhythm
stories.desc: In living cells, tiny molecules can generate coordinated motion across distances thousands of times larger than the molecules themselves. How such small movements give rise to coordinated motion over much larger distances is still not fully understood.

stories.title: Detecting Blocked Rain Gauges for Reliable Weather Data
stories.desc: When rain gauges are blocked or broken, they present faulty data. Various methods to detect faulty instruments may work better in different regions, according to new research.

stories.title: Changing Arctic Waters Reshape Life from the Seafloor to the Coastlines
stories.desc: More than a decade of observations has revealed the many ways that the Arctic Ocean’s chemistry is changing, affecting the marine life and human communities that rely on its resources.
